source: Quix, Geschichte der ehemaligen Reichsabtei Burtscheid, Urkunde 162, S. 396–398
entries.summary: Clais von Rosenberg verkauft der Abtei Burtscheid 7 Morgen Land in dem Broich und bei dem Steinweg zu Wetzauen. Mit 7 Siegeln (Aachener Schöffen).

entries.english: We, the Richter and Schöffen of the venerable court of Aachen, named below, make known to all people with this letter and declare publicly that there appeared before us Nicolaus von Rosenberg, who, of his good intent and free will, in lawful time, when he well could, has sold and sells hereditarily and free of encumbrance to Hans van den Yseren, for the use and benefit of Vrouwe Rikarde van Ulpich, Abbess of Burtscheid, and of the whole convent of Burtscheid, seven morgen of land. Five of these morgen lie in one piece in the Bruch at Wetzschauwen, beside the land of Willem Bendel, and owe below sixteen pennies and in addition the tithe; the other two morgen lie by the Steinweg, between the land of the said convent of Burtscheid, and owe nothing more than the tithe. All this land is burdened or encumbered with nothing more than is stated above. Clais, Hans in den Ziendehoff, Clais his lawful son, and Willem Bendel van Wetzschauwen acknowledged and promised to Hans van den Yseren, for the use and benefit of the said Vrouwe Rikarde and the said convent of Burtscheid, to warrant it within the year and outside the year, and manfully, for a stated sum of money, namely 255 marks of Aachen currency, which Hans van den Yseren has fully and completely paid to Clais on behalf of the said Vrouwe Rikarde and the convent of Burtscheid; and Clais acknowledges before us that he is fully satisfied. Accordingly Nicolaus von Rosenberg has divested himself of possession and use of the said land and of all legal claim or demand that he formerly had or still has to it, and has renounced them without complaint and completely, with mouth and with straw, hereditarily and free of encumbrance, for the use and benefit of Vrouwe Rikarde and of the whole convent of Burtscheid. Furthermore the sureties Clais, Hans, Clais and Wilhem promise Hans van den Yseren, for the use and benefit of Vrouwe Rikarde and the whole convent of Burtscheid, to warrant the land year and day according to the law and custom of the city of Aachen, and to settle all legal claims concerning it, without deceit, saving the rights of the lords of the fief. In witness of the truth we, Wilhem van Raide, Richter, Reynart van Moircken, Hans van Pont, Heinrich van der Linden, Arnold Volmer, Wernher Bertolf, Heynrich Chorus and Gerart Lewe, Schöffen of the said court of Aachen, have, at the request of the parties on both sides, hung our seals on this letter, which was given in the year of our Lord 1381, on the sixteenth day of the month of February. [Editorial note: of the 8 seals, 2 are badly damaged.]
